topic: Claude skills from zero to your first one, in lessons that each point to the guide that goes deeper
audience: Professionals who use Claude every day but paste the same instructions again and again
goal: Make and test a first skill safely, using the free guides on mojeedabisiga.com/learn
notes: A skill is a small folder of instructions (sometimes scripts and templates) that teaches Claude one job the way you want it done. Install it once; Claude picks it up whenever a request needs it.
Every skill has one required file, SKILL.md. Its name is also the command you can type, such as /learn-anything; its description says what it does and when to use it.
Skills load in layers: always just the name and description; the instructions when a request matches; extra files only if needed. So you can install many without slowing Claude down.

The ten skills Mojeed wrote for the people he teaches: learn-anything (teaches any topic step by step from what you already know), quiz-me (turns notes into practice questions, one at a time), research-brief (a short sourced brief with a confidence level for each finding), news-explainer (what happened, why it matters, who it affects), job-application (tailors a CV and cover letter to a specific job ad, honestly), linkedin-post (posts in your own voice), meeting-to-actions (decisions, actions with owners and deadlines, follow-up email), presentation-planner (one message per slide, speaker notes), check-the-numbers (profiles the file and proves the answer first), skill-maker (drafts, checks and zips your own skill).

Install: 1) download the zip, don't unzip it; 2) Settings → Capabilities → turn on 'Create and edit files' (older layout: 'Code execution and file creation'); 3) Customize → Skills → + → Create skill → Upload a skill; 4) check the switch is on.

Using a skill: Claude uses it by itself when a request matches. To be sure, name it in the request (for example: 'Use my weekly-report skill on these notes'). In Claude Code you can also type / and pick it.
Claude's own directory: Customize → Skills → + → Browse skills. It includes skills from partners such as Notion, Figma and Atlassian, built to work with their connectors.

How skills compare: custom instructions apply to every conversation; projects apply to the chats inside that project; connectors give Claude access to other apps and data when it needs them; a skill applies only when a request needs it, in any chat.
Where skills work: Claude on the web and in the desktop app (every plan, once code execution is on), Claude Code, the Claude add-ins for Excel, PowerPoint, Word and Outlook, and Cowork.

Making your own: SKILL.md starts with its name and description between two lines of dashes (for example name: weekly-report). Zip the folder, not the files inside it: the zip must contain weekly-report/SKILL.md. A skill is worth making once you've explained the same thing to Claude three times.

Safety: a skill can contain code that runs when Claude uses it, so treat an unknown skill like an unknown app. Read every file before you switch a skill on. Never put passwords, API keys or personal data in a skill.

Rules for making a skill: name in lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens, 64 characters at most; description says what it does and when to use it, 200 characters at most in the Claude apps; instructions under 500 lines. Test with 3 requests that should use it and 2 that shouldn't; if Claude misses one, improve the description first.

Claude Code: unzip into ~/.claude/skills/ for every project, or a project's .claude/skills/ folder (commit it); /skills lists what's installed. Team plans: skills on by default; Enterprise: an owner turns them on first.
Mojeed's website: https://mojeedabisiga.com/ (his biography, work, speaking and contact).
Claude decides when to use a skill from its description alone. Description: what it does and when to use it, third person, 200 characters at most in the Claude apps, no tags in angle brackets.
Mojeed's free guides are at https://mojeedabisiga.com/learn (the pages are listed in learn_catalog.json).
